1.why: Headings and body text use a clean, legible sans-serif with comfortable line height and whitespace, although letter spacing appears standard rather than explicitly generous.

2.why: Instructions are short sentence-case lines with no italics, no all-caps prose, and no dense paragraphs (the only all-caps string is the setup secret itself, not instruction text).

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow centred column with large buttons that should translate well to a phone screen, though only desktop-width screenshots were provided to confirm.

4.why: Each screen's instructions are one or two short sentences, but phrases like 'MFA enrolment' and 'time-bound code' assume some familiarity with the concepts.

5.why: The six-digit code field is blank with no placeholder or sample showing the expected format; only the prefilled email and phone values demonstrate an input shape.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a couple of short lines before acting, and the longest text block is two lines.

7.why: The 32-character setup secret is shown as static text with no copy button, and the user is explicitly directed to choose manual entry and type it into their authenticator app.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative is offered anywhere; manual entry of the secret is the only provisioning path shown.

9.why: The inputs are plain text fields with no visible indication of autofill or password-manager support, such as a one-time-code hint or autofill trigger.

10.why: Each screen has a clear heading and a single high-contrast blue primary button, but there is no progress indicator showing which enrolment step the user is on.

11.why: Every screen presents one dominant primary button, although the setup screen combines an off-page task (register the secret in the app) with the on-page code entry.

12.why: A developer-styled log records what happened in technical language ('Authenticator provisioning created'), and the next screen implies what to do next, but there is no plain user-facing statement of outcome plus next step.

13.why: Retry is possible after the error since the Confirm button remains active, but there are no reveal/hide toggles or any way to re-request a code.

14.why: The red message 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' avoids blaming the user but does not state the actual problem (wrong or expired code) or a concrete fix beyond retrying.

15.why: No countdown or reading time limit is visible on any screen, but the code is described as time-bound with no indication of a generous entry window or ability to extend time.
